maya-glm-dual-xtx.context_scaling_note: Each point: a fresh load, the public prompt bytes of the DeepSeek rows (GLM counts fewer tokens for the same text), thinking off, 256-token cap (answers used 52-61 tokens), zero cached input. 2K-64K at a 131,072-token allocation, 128K-240K at 262,144, 480K at 524,288; the 128K prompt read at 907.1 tok/s and decoded at 55.8 at 131,072. The retrieval filler routes to few experts, so its prefill is faster than real text (long_context).

maya-ds4-exl3-dual-xtx.context_scaling_note: Eleven matched five-phrase prompts, three fresh loads per point; the curve is each metric's median and per_load retains all repeats. Frozen expert profile, no saved conversation, thinking off, 256-token cap (all answers used 64 tokens), zero cached input. EXL3 allocates 1,048,576 tokens; the historical GSQ, Maya-S and Maya-XS curves allocate 524,288. Separate 520,000- and 1,040,000-token checks are retained. Different generated text and draft acceptance; no causal or stream-matched decode claim.

maya_bench.procedure: Frozen Project Maya v1.1.28 maya.py --bench procedure on the installed E+ engine: three 256-token greedy answers, thinking off; decode is their arithmetic mean, followed by fixed 2,048- and 8,192-token prompts. One engine load; the published fixture is unchanged.

One current median curve with all repetitions retained. Different generated text and draft acceptance; no causal or stream-matched decode claim.
